fn.en: Complain about something you bought and ask for a refund — in a shop and by email.

lines: I’d like to [return|replace|refund] this, please. It doesn’t work. 💸
Have you got the [receipt|refund|delivery]? — Yes, here it is. 🧾
I’m afraid we can’t give you a refund, but we can [exchange|complain|apologise] it. 🔁
It arrived [damaged|damage|damaging] — there’s a scratch across the front. 💥
We’re very sorry for the [inconvenience|inconvenient|convenience] and we’ll sort it out. 🙏

items.q: The machine is broken and doesn’t work: it’s ___.
A part is not in the box: a part is ___.
The paper that promises a free repair for two years: a ___.
To say sorry, formally: to ___.
To give the customer a new one instead: to ___ it.
The trouble the mistake caused you: the ___.

sub.en: Look at the phrases. Which ones are the customer’s, and which ones are the shop’s?

items.q: ___ return this, please.
items.why: I’d like to… is the polite way to open a complaint. I want… is understood, but it is blunt.

items.q: It ___ properly.
___ a refund, please?
It ___ damaged.
“___ we can’t give a refund without the receipt.”
items.why: I’m afraid… softens a refusal. It is the shop’s phrase, not the customer’s.

items.q: “We ___ for the inconvenience.”
“We’ll ___ it as soon as possible.”
I ___ it three weeks ago and I ___ used it twice.
items.why: RECYCLED: a finished time takes the Past Simple; a life-to-now count takes the present perfect.

acts.title: To: orders@… Subject: Order 88214 — damaged on arrival
text: I ordered a table lamp from your website on 3 October (order number 88214) and it arrived yesterday.

Unfortunately the box was open at one end and the lamp inside is damaged. There is a long scratch across the base and the glass part is missing altogether. I have not used it and I have kept all the packaging.
I have been a customer for six years and I have never had a problem before, so I am sure this is not typical.
Could I have a refund, please? If a refund is not possible, I would accept a replacement, but I would prefer my money back at this point.
I have attached a photograph of the damage and a copy of the receipt. Could you let me know what you need from me?
I look forward to hearing from you.

write.q: Write a complaint email about something you bought that arrived damaged or stopped working: 8–10 lines. Follow the model’s six moves, and use at least four of its phrases: Unfortunately… / I have not used it / Could I have a refund, please? / I would accept… / I look forward to hearing from you / Yours faithfully.
write.model: Dear Sir or Madam, I ordered a pair of headphones from your website on 12 November (order 41307) and they arrived on Friday. Unfortunately the left one does not work at all. I have not used them outside the house and I have kept the box and all the packaging. I have been a customer for four years and this is the first problem I have had. Could I have a refund, please? If a refund is not possible, I would accept a replacement pair. I have attached a copy of the receipt. Could you let me know what you need from me? I look forward to hearing from you. Yours faithfully, Marat Zhaksybek

speak.q: Play both parts out loud: as the customer, return something and ask for a refund; as the shop, refuse the refund politely, offer an exchange and apologise.
speak.model: I’d like to return this, please. It doesn’t work — it stopped after a week. Could I have a refund? — I’m afraid we can’t refund it without a receipt, but we can exchange it. We apologise for the inconvenience.
